applications.comparison: The receiving model is explicitly projective and relatively minimal with a zero section and a unique I12 fibre. This matches assumptions (1.1). Its rank13 trivial lattice is generated by O,F and the eleven nonidentity I12 components, matching T in Theorem1.3; the NS quotient identifies its section group.
The same elliptic surface satisfies assumptions (1.1). Pullback Pic0(C) to Pic0(E) is the exact isomorphism supplied, consistent with the printed Leray irregularity calculation.

The primary I_b correction i(b-j)/b for i<j, with symmetry and diagonal i(b-i)/b, is exactly min(i,j)-ij/12 when b=12. The receiving height pairing uses the same zero section and component indices; reversing4 to8 leaves the displayed pair corrections unchanged. No fresh execution or independent theorem check is claimed.

applications.primary_locator: Proposition8.12, equation(8.25), p.231; supporting narrow divisor formula(8.23), p.230
applications.comparison: The finite multisection gives a degree d function-field extension. Proposition8.12 multiplies the height of the pulled-back P by d. The receiving line is the narrow Poincare divisor up to a base line; its negative self-intersection equals the height by the projected-divisor formula, and a base line pairs trivially with a fibre-degree-zero line. This authenticates the cited application scope; it does not independently recheck the torsor construction.

limitations: This is exact primary-source and application-scope authentication. It adds no independent or computational check credit, and does not certify portions of the receiving proofs outside the cited applications.
